record.context_brief: Effect of monomial order on cone filtrations
record.original_question: When cone filtrations between Σ_{n+1,2d} and P_{n+1,2d} are built by ordering the monomials of I_{n+1,d}, which structural properties of the chosen monomial order determine whether adjacent cones become equal or remain strictly separated, and how do those order-theoretic properties control the resulting pattern of equalities and inequalities in the filtration?

evidence.quote: The Example 3.2 above illustrates that different monomial orders may lead to different behaviours of inclusions in corresponding cone filtrations (similar to (5) and (8)) that can be constructed by our method.
Therefore, it would be interesting to investigate which properties of a monomial order influence the occurence of cone equalities and inequalities, and how?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n,d be positive integers. Write P_{n+1,2d} for the cone of real homogeneous polynomials of degree 2d in n+1 variables that are nonnegative on R^{n+1}, and Σ_{n+1,2d} for its subcone of sums of squares of homogeneous polynomials of degree d. Let I_{n+1,d} denote the set of monomials of degree d in n+1 variables, so that the squares of these monomials span a natural subspace inside Σ_{n+1,2d}.

Given a monomial order ≺ on the polynomial ring R[x_0,...,x_n], list the monomials of I_{n+1,d} in increasing order as m_1 ≺ m_2 ≺ ... ≺ m_N. Using this ordering, construct a nested filtration of convex cones
   C_0 ⊆ C_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ C_N
interpolating between Σ_{n+1,2d} and P_{n+1,2d}, where C_k is obtained from C_{k-1} by adjoining the kth monomial m_k in the prescribed way (so that C_0 = Σ_{n+1,2d} and C_N = P_{n+1,2d}, or another fixed pair as dictated by the construction).

Problem. Identify the order-theoretic and combinatorial properties of the monomial order ≺ (for instance, whether it is lexicographic, graded lexicographic, graded reverse lexicographic, a weight order, an elimination order, the placement of the smallest/largest variable, compatibility with symmetries, etc.) that determine, for each index k, whether the inclusion C_{k-1} ⊆ C_k is an equality or strict. Describe explicitly how these properties of ≺ control the resulting pattern of equalities and strict inclusions in the filtration C_0 ⊆ C_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ C_N.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a direction for further investigation about how monomial-order properties affect cone equalities/inequalities in filtrations between the SOS and PSD cones. No published resolution was found in a web search; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Study of the cone of sums of squares plus sums of nonnegative circuit forms
status_evidence.snippet: Study of cones between SOS and PSD via additional generators; no resolution of monomial-order effect on cone filtrations.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on intermediate cones, but does not resolve the dependence on monomial order.

status_evidence.title: Basis selection for SOS programs via facial reduction
status_evidence.snippet: Monomial basis selection for SOS uses chains of faces of the SOS cone.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic perspective on monomial selection, distinct from a structural characterization of monomial-order effects on filtrations.
